issues.display_title: Issue #626: Issue: Unable to save the project after importing a multi-floor Mapthru
issues.main_description_html:
Asset test:

c8238b8b8086d43ed23eb5b3a80269d0b77ce143.zip

  • Set the default for automatic floor mapping and “same height” in imported projects to “false”

Note From Developer

Fixed in #654 (development cb6ce8a) → main 8ae66b9.

Root cause. Saving posts the whole canvasData through a Server Action, and Next caps that body at 1 MB by default. The 36-floor export attached here converts to ~1.66 MB of levels, so every save — toolbar button and 2-second autosave alike — returned 500 Body exceeded 1 MB limit (E394). The Go API already accepted 50 MB; the frontend was the only ceiling.

Fix. serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "16mb" plus proxyClientMaxBodySize: "20mb". The second one matters: proxy.ts matches every route, so Next clones each request body for it, and past that cap (10 MB by default) the body is truncated, not rejected — the handler then dies on half a payload with Unterminated string in JSON. The two caps are deliberately unequal so the action rejects first and says so by name. Verified against a production build: 15 MB → 200, 17 MB → 500 Body exceeded 16mb limit.

Checklist item — automatic floor mapping / same height default to false on import: done. Auto-naming was on by default and nothing turned it off for imported floors, so all 36 were renamed to Floor N the moment a floor modal mounted. Every import path now pins both toggles off, and projects imported before this heal on load rather than needing a re-import.

Worth knowing, not fixed here:

  • Autosave sends canvasData twice per cycle (updateProject then saveFloorplanAction, both writing the same canvas_data column) — 3493 KB where 1755 KB would do.
  • DB_DRIVER defaults to mysql in src/config/database.go, where gorm:"type:text" is 64 KB. Only the deployed env var keeps production on Postgres.
  • The production edge (client_max_body_size) has not been checked against a >1 MB save. Worth one POST after deploy before closing.

issues.display_title: Issue #656: chore(security): remove the DISABLE_AUTH bypass and developer mode
issues.main_description_html:
Both mechanisms are meant to be dev-only conveniences. Neither is, and both ship to production.

Developer mode

src/proxy.ts:24-28 turns devModeActive on when either the x-developer-mode request header matches DEVELOPER_MODE_CODE or the dev_mode=1 cookie is present. That flag then skips the whole access-control block: the signed-out redirect (:34), protected paths (:40), the emailVerified gate (:53) and the support-role check (:61).

The cookie is set without httpOnly (:90), is unsigned, and is never verified. Measured on a local dev server with no session at all:

/dashboard  no cookie          → 307 /login
/dashboard  Cookie: dev_mode=1 → 200      ← route guard skipped

Blast radius is limited — every data path still needs a session token server-side, so the page renders empty, and proxy.ts:91-92 deletes the forged cookie on the way out, which is why /dev still 404s under a forged cookie. The header path is the unlimited one: anyone holding DEVELOPER_MODE_CODE reaches /start and /editor with an unverified or absent session, because neither page carries its own auth() check.

src/actions/dev.ts is gated on the same cookie and does nothing less than decrypt an arbitrary NextAuth JWE with NEXTAUTH_SECRET.

DISABLE_AUTH

src/lib/devAuth.ts gates on NODE_ENV !== "production", so the flag itself is inert in a deployed build. The local stand-in routes it was written for are not gated by anything:

POST /api/project   (no auth check anywhere in the file)
  → 200 {"id":"27047cf9-…","name":"unauthenticated write test","status":"draft"}
  → wrote /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap/projects/27047cf9-….json

src/app/api/project/route.ts, src/app/api/project/[id]/route.ts and src/app/api/live/[key]/route.ts compile into every build and check nothing. An unauthenticated caller can make the server create a directory and write attacker-named JSON files, one per request.

The bypass also no longer does what it advertises — /api/files stopped serving the local /tmp copies, /api/predict forwards upstream regardless, saveFloorplanAction has no local branch, and getToken() returning "" sends Bearer on 12 call sites. It is strictly worse than not setting the flag.

Scope

Delete both. Files removed: src/lib/devAuth.ts, src/actions/dev.ts, src/app/dev/page.tsx, src/components/dev/SessionTokenDecoder.tsx, src/app/api/project/route.ts, src/app/api/project/[id]/route.ts, src/app/api/live/[key]/route.ts, plus their tests. Edited: src/proxy.ts, src/actions/projects.ts, src/lib/server/session.ts, src/app/api/upload/route.ts, src/app/api/predict/route.ts, src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx, src/components/editor/preview/useDirectionMapLayers.ts, .env.example.

The nav-grid debug overlay ("round dots" on preview) goes with it — it is the only cosmetic thing developer mode unlocked.

Acceptance

  • No route or action grants access on a request header, an unsigned cookie, or an env flag
  • /api/project* and /api/live/* local stand-ins gone; no unauthenticated write path remains
  • Regression test: a protected path with dev_mode=1 and no session still redirects to login
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit, pnpm build green
  • DEVELOPER_MODE_CODE / DISABLE_AUTH removed from .env.example; confirm they are unset on the deploy host

issues.display_title: Issue #662: Integrate design/wizard-mappedin into development: preserve imported buildings on Add More Floors + per-building floor ordering
issues.main_description_html:
Frontend integration task for #650 (PRD) / #657 (design + spec). Design work is finished on design/wizard-mappedin; this issue carries it onto development.

PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-wizard-mappedin-add-more-floors-building-safety/prd.md (branch product-docs)
Design branch: design/wizard-mappedin
Spec issue: #657 · PRD issue: #650 · Related: #643

Problem

Mappedin imports can contain several buildings. The review modal groups them, but the grouping dies one step later: when the user picks Add More Floors instead of Continue to Editor, imported floors are flattened into one project-wide list. Reordering then looks harmless but can silently move a floor into the wrong building, and a manually uploaded image floor has no clear home.

Heads-up: design/mappedin-import-building-grouping (#643) never landed on development

#643 is closed as completed, but its helpers exist only on design/mappedin-import-building-grouping:

  • src/lib/mappedin-import/groupBuildings.ts — absent from origin/development
  • src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts — absent from origin/development
  • src/components/setup/import-mappedin/BuildingGroupSection.tsx — absent from origin/development

design/wizard-mappedin carries both #643 and the new wizard work, so this integration covers #643 as well — no separate integrate issue needed. Nothing needs to be written from scratch; mergeImportIntoProject and groupFloorsByBuilding are already pure and tested on the branch.

Scope

  1. Add More Floors — imported buildings and per-floor building membership survive the jump into the upload step.
  2. Manual/image floors — default to Main Building, shown as a normal building group once it has floors.
  3. Floor ordering step — grouped by building for multi-building projects; reorder within a group only.
  4. Continue to Editor — the editor opens with exactly the structure the wizard showed.

Requirements

Same table as #657 (R1–R16). Musts in short: preserve imported buildings (R1) and per-floor membership (R2); manual floors → Main Building (R3, R4); grouped ordering (R5, R6) that never changes membership (R7); readable names with Building N / Main Building fallbacks (R8, R9); editor handoff preserves structure and order (R11); removals stay scoped to one building (R12, R13); single-building imports stay lightweight (R14); image-only flow unchanged (R15); no raw ids or file internals in the UI (R16).

Where membership is lost today (verified on origin/development)

  1. src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts:64 — floorStacks.flatMap((stack) => stack.floors ?? []). A Mappedin floor stack is a building; every stack collapses into one flat floorIds list. Nothing downstream can recover it.
  2. src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:358-370 — the returned canvasData is {levels, coordSpace, mapRotationDeg, mapOffsetX/Y}: never sets buildings, never stamps buildingId.
  3. src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:186-189 (Add More Floors) — raw level prepend, no Building record created, no buildingId stamped; paired with addImportedFloorsToWizard (runImport.ts:59). Every imported floor from every batch lands in the one implicit default building.
  4. Siblings on the same data — fixing only #3 leaves these flattening: StepUploadFloor.tsx:135 (Continue to Editor replaces canvasData wholesale), StepGenerate.tsx:90 (createBlankCanvasData on the step-4 exit), src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:169-175 (force-stamps every imported level with selectedBuildingId), src/hooks/useDigitalTwinExport.ts:62 (twin rebuild keeps {levels, coordSpace} only).

Data shape: FloorConfig (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:24-32) has no building field. Membership is LevelData.buildingId? (:276) plus CanvasData.buildings? (:303), so it rides save/undo/publish for free. levelsInBuilding (src/lib/editor/levels.ts:117-128) resolves unstamped levels to buildings[0] — everything downstream already reads through it, so no downstream changes are needed once levels are stamped. Imported floors are local component state only (StepUploadFloor.tsx:53) and are not persisted by src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts.

Files (from design/wizard-mappedin, 39 files / ~2.3k insertions incl. PRD docs)

Port as-is (new, pure, already tested): src/lib/mappedin-import/{groupBuildings,mergeIntoProject}.ts, src/lib/wizard/floorBuildings.ts, src/components/setup/import-mappedin/BuildingGroupSection.tsx, src/components/setup/step-list-floor/{BuildingFloorGroup,FloorStack}.tsx, src/components/setup/step-upload/UploadedGroup.tsx, src/components/setup/step-list-floor/useFloorReorder.ts, plus their __tests__.

Re-apply call sites by hand on current development: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx, src/components/setup/StepListFloor.tsx, src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx, src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts, src/components/editor/AddLevelModal.tsx, src/lib/mappedin/{parse,types}.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/{detectSource,extractFloors,runImport}.ts, src/lib/editor/levels.ts (fillMissingLevels), src/store/mapStore/floorsSlice.ts, src/components/setup/import-mappedin/{FloorListSection,ImportSummaryModal,ImportModalActions,types}.

Call shape: mergeImportIntoProject({ groups: groupFloorsByBuilding(importResult), levels: src.canvasData.levels, canvasData, floorConfigs, keepIds: true[, prepend: true] }) → setCanvasData / setFloorConfigs / selectBuilding(staged.buildingId) / setActiveLevelId(staged.levelId).

Merge hazards

  • The branch forked at c8a9806; development is 11 commits ahead, and both StepUploadFloor.tsx and useAddLevel.ts changed in that window.
  • keepImportedFloorSettings() (from the #626 autosave fix) exists nowhere on design/wizard-mappedin. The existing calls at StepUploadFloor.tsx:141 and useAddLevel.ts:197 on development must survive the port — do not take the branch's component versions wholesale.
  • mergeIntoProject.ts:65-70 guard: a project with levels but zero Building records has them in the implicit default; appending an imported building would make the import buildings[0] and silently adopt them. The helper materializes a real "Untitled building" record and stamps existing levels first — keep that behavior and its test.

Tests

  • Multi-building import stays grouped after Add More Floors.
  • Imported floors keep their original building membership.
  • A manual/image floor added after import lands in Main Building.
  • Step 3 reorder changes order only within one building.
  • Cross-building reorder does not change membership.
  • Removing an imported floor does not disturb other buildings.
  • Removing a manual floor does not disturb imported buildings.
  • Continue to Editor preserves imported buildings, Main Building, and floor order.
  • Regression: single-building import stays simple.
  • Regression: image-only wizard flow unchanged.
  • Keep the ported groupBuildings / mergeIntoProject / levels / floorBuildings / useFloorReorder suites green.

Acceptance checklist

  • Add More Floors preserves imported Mappedin buildings.
  • Add More Floors preserves imported floor membership.
  • Manual/image floors added after import go to Main Building.
  • Main Building is visible when manual floors exist in a multi-building project.
  • Floor ordering is grouped by building for multi-building projects.
  • Reorder works within a building group and never moves floors between buildings.
  • Continue to Editor preserves imported buildings, Main Building, and floor order within each building.
  • Removing floors does not disturb unrelated buildings.
  • Single-building imports remain simple; image-only wizard flows remain unchanged.
  • Copy is clear, plain, and non-technical.
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, and vitest pass.

Manual verification

  1. New project → import a Mappedin file with at least two buildings → Add More Floors.
  2. Add one image floor manually, continue to the floor ordering step.
  3. Confirm imported floors are grouped under their imported buildings and the manual floor sits under Main Building.
  4. Reorder floors inside one imported building — the floor stays in that building.
  5. Continue to the editor and confirm the same building + floor structure.
  6. Repeat with a single-building import, then with an image-only flow (no Mappedin) — both unchanged.

Out of scope

Moving floors between buildings in the wizard · a full building manager in the wizard · renaming buildings or imported floor names in the review modal · guessing which imported building a manual floor belongs to · billing, permissions, collaboration, publishing, viewer, embed · new import formats.

RESULT

Branch: feature/662-integrate-design-wizard-mappedin · Commit: a99b08f · 38 files, +1717/-326

design/wizard-mappedin ported onto development file by file (git merge is off-limits in this repo). 32 files were taken as-is; three were hand-merged because development had moved too: StepUploadFloor.tsx, useAddLevel.ts, floorsSlice.ts — the only delta against the design branch in those three is development's keepImportedFloorSettings (#626), restored at all four call sites. This also carries #643, which was closed but never reached development.

What changed

  • Both wizard exits — Continue to Editor and Add More Floors — stage the reviewed groups through mergeImportIntoProject: each imported building becomes its own Building record and every level is stamped with its own buildingId, never the selected one (R1/R2).
  • Manual/image floors go to Main Building (R3/R4); step 2 shows it as a group only once an import has put other buildings on screen, so the image-only flow is untouched (R14/R15).
  • Step 3 orders floors inside a building group; reorderWithinBuildings keeps each building's slots, so a drag across a boundary reorders within the floor's own building instead of moving it (R5/R6/R7).
  • fillMissingLevels replaces createBlankCanvasData on the step-4 exit, so generating no longer discards staged buildings and geometry (R11).
  • Removing a floor drops its level with its config, and an emptied group stops rendering rather than lingering (R12/R13).

Two defects found while porting, both fixed

useDigitalTwinExport.openInEditor deleted the structure the wizard had just built. It rebuilt canvasData as {levels, coordSpace}, dropping canvasData.buildings and every buildingId, and rebuilt floorConfigs from dt.levels alone. An imported Mappedin floor has serverPath: "", so it never scans, never enters the twin — and was deleted by "Open Editor" after Generate, undoing the preservation work rebuildTwin had done thirty lines earlier. Now mergeTwinIntoCanvas (pure, extracted, tested) lays each scanned level over the one already stored, keeps the floors the twin does not carry, spreads the rest of canvasData, and orders levels by floorConfigs.

Main Building was identified by name. fillMissingLevels picked the manual bucket with b.name === "Main Building". A Mappedin floor stack can legitimately be named that, and the import then absorbed every uploaded image floor while the UI still labelled those floors "floor plans you added here" — R4 failing silently. Building.imported now marks import-created records, and the bucket is found by that flag in fillMissingLevels, groupFloorConfigsByBuilding and BuildingFloorGroup.

Both were found by an adversarial review pass over the staged diff: 19 candidate findings, 17 refuted against the code, these 2 confirmed.

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 137 files, 1085 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (was 1080 — 5 new regression tests in levels.test.ts and useDigitalTwinExport.test.ts, on top of the ported groupBuildings, mergeIntoProject and floorBuildings suites).

Manual QA from the checklist above still needs a real two-building Mappedin export in a browser.

issues.display_title: Issue #665: Wizard: imported Mappedin floors dead-end at step 3 — Continue is disabled, the step-4 checklist never matches, and Generate reports them as failures
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up to #662, found while recording its demo. After Add More Floors, the wizard cannot be finished: step 3's Continue never enables, so the imported project never reaches step 4 or the editor.

This is pre-existing, not introduced by #662 — the old addImportedFloorsToWizard produced the same configs — but #662 is what makes the path worth walking, and #657's manual verification (steps 5–10) runs straight into it.

Evidence

Recorded against development at .playwright-mcp/demo/662/video-662-wizard-buildings.mp4 (see check-68.png): step 3 shows the three building groups correctly, and underneath sits "Every floor needs a name and an uploaded plan to continue." with Continue greyed out.

Root cause

An imported Mappedin floor carries geometry instead of an uploaded image, so its FloorConfig.serverPath is "" (runImport.ts toWizardFloorConfig). Three places treat "no uploaded image" as "not a real floor":

# Where What happens
1 src/components/setup/StepListFloor.tsx:34 — allFloorConfigsReady(configs) (src/lib/projects/wizardProject.ts:61) requires a non-empty serverPath on every config Step 3 Continue is permanently disabled once any imported floor is staged. Hard block.
2 src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:236 — buildChecklist({ floorCount, uploadedImageCount: uploadedFiles.length }), matched in step-generate/checklist.ts as floorCount === uploadedImageCount With 3 imported + 1 uploaded floor it is 4 vs 1 — the readiness card can never match, and shows the "add floors" message on a project that has floors.
3 src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:170 feeds every floor id to runGeneration; generateFloor (:138) throws "…: no uploaded file — cannot scan" when serverPath is empty Every imported floor is reported as a generation failure, though there is nothing to scan — it is already geometry.

Proposed fix

A floor is ready when it has a name and either an uploaded plan or its own geometry (a level in canvasData with content). Concretely:

  1. Gate step 3 on that rule instead of allFloorConfigsReady, so imported floors count as ready.
  2. Feed the checklist the number of floors that are ready — uploaded images plus imported floors — so it matches a mixed project.
  3. Have Generate scan only the floors that have an uploaded plan, and leave imported floors alone rather than failing them.

Image-only projects keep today's behavior exactly: with no imported floors, every rule collapses to the current one.

Acceptance

  • After Add More Floors with a mixed project, step 3 Continue is enabled.
  • Step 4's checklist matches for a mixed project (imported + uploaded).
  • Generate scans only uploaded-image floors; imported floors are not reported as failures.
  • Imported floors still reach the editor with their buildings and order intact (#662 R11).
  • A floor with neither an image nor geometry still blocks Continue.
  • Image-only wizard flow unchanged (R15); single-building import unchanged (R14).
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest green, with tests for the mixed-project gate.

Manual verification

  1. New project → import a two-building Mappedin export → Add More Floors.
  2. Upload one image floor → continue to step 3.
  3. Confirm Continue is enabled and step 4 opens with a matching checklist.
  4. Generate: the uploaded floor scans, the imported floors are left as they are and reported as neither failed nor scanned.
  5. Continue to the editor: buildings, Main Building, and per-building order all intact.
  6. Repeat an image-only run and confirm nothing changed.

RESULT

Branch: fix/665-imported-floors-wizard-gates · Commit: 62af1f9 · 8 files, +165/-11

A floor is ready when it has a name and a plan — an uploaded image or its own geometry. The rule lives once in src/lib/projects/wizardProject.ts (floorHasGeometry, scannableFloorIds, allFloorConfigsReady(configs, canvasData)) and is applied at all three gates. Calling it without canvasData keeps the old image-only rule verbatim, so an image-only wizard is untouched.

  • StepListFloor.tsx — Step 3's Continue accepts imported floors; the hint now reads "a plan — uploaded or imported".
  • checklist.ts / vm.ts / RequirementChecklist.tsx — new importedFloorCount counts towards matches, and the card grows an Imported stat only for a project that has one.
  • StepGenerate.tsx — only floors with an uploaded image are seeded into the run, so imported floors are no longer reported as "no uploaded file — cannot scan". rebuildTwin already preserved their levels.

A blank placeholder level still has no geometry and still blocks Continue.

Verified in the browser, against this branch

STEP 3 Continue disabled? false                       (hint gone)
STEP 4 checklist: Project Floors · MATCH · CONFIGURED 4 floors · UPLOADED 1 image · IMPORTED 3 floors
Generate:  0 "no uploaded file" failures — progress list = [Floor 4] only
Editor:    building options = [Airport Demo, Community Centre Demo, Main Building]
           opens on Airport Demo → Level 1, 65 objects, "No floors yet" absent

Fixture: the two-building Mappedin export from the #662 demo plus one uploaded image floor. That last line is #662 R11 confirmed end to end — this path could not be walked at all before the fix.

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 137 files, 1093 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (+8 tests: the readiness rule with imported / mixed / blank / no-canvas cases, and the checklist's imported count).

issues.display_title: Issue #663: Map placement scopes: All Buildings / Selected Building / Selected Floor (PRD #591 R23-R38)
issues.main_description_html:
Editor Map placement tools name their target inconsistently, and one of the three options only exists as a workaround.

Today alignmentScope is "all" | "active" | "project" (src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:35) and the buttons read "All floors" / "Active floor" / "Project" (src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx:393-405). "All floors" actually means the selected building, and "Project" appears only while a stranded project-wide frame exists (#572) — so the user cannot tell what a drag will move before moving it.

PRD #591 R23-R38 fixes the vocabulary: exactly three scopes, the same three words wherever a placement change starts, and the project frame IS "All Buildings" rather than a fourth hidden option.

Scope Frame it writes
All Buildings canvasData.mapRotationDeg / mapScale / mapOffsetX/Y — every building moves together, relative positions preserved
Selected Building the selected building's mapTransform (#548)
Selected Floor the active level's mapTransform (#504)

Design branch design/editor-map-outer-buildings already carries this work; it merges clean on these files.

Scope

  • src/lib/map/placement.ts — PlacementScope type + SCOPE_LABEL; drop projectFrameStranded / effectiveAlignmentScope
  • src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts — alignmentScope: PlacementScope, default "building"
  • src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx — scope column, tooltips, reset copy
  • src/components/editor/toolbar/MapScopeButton.tsx (new) + EditorBottomToolbar.tsx — scope picker and drag tooltip
  • src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx — drag target + move-mode hint read the new scope
  • src/lib/map/__tests__/placement.test.ts

Out of scope: outer building shells and click-to-select — separate task.

Acceptance

  • Exactly three user-facing scopes: All Buildings, Selected Building, Selected Floor (R23, R38)
  • Drag, rotate, scale, nudge and reset all read the same active scope (R36)
  • All Buildings reset clears only the project frame; Selected Building reset only that building's mapTransform; Selected Floor reset only the active level's (R27, R31, R35)
  • Tooltips and the move-mode hint name the active scope (R37)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Branch: feature/663-map-placement-scopes (from development) · Commit: 34ff1f3

alignmentScope is now PlacementScope — allBuildings | building | floor — with one SCOPE_LABEL map that every surface reads, so the drag tooltip, the transform popup's trigger and the move-mode hint cannot drift apart (R37). The project-wide frame IS All Buildings; projectFrameStranded / effectiveAlignmentScope are gone with it, and so is the fourth "Project" button that used to appear and vanish on its own (R38).

The scope moved out of the transform popup into its own toolbar button (MapScopeButton), because R23's point is that the user knows what will move before reaching for a tool. Drag, rotate, scale, nudge and reset all read the one value (R36), and each reset still clears only its own frame (R27/R31/R35) — a Selected Building reset never touches the derived georeferencing a Mappedin import writes to the project frame.

Files:

 src/lib/map/placement.ts                         |  56 ++++-----
 src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts                |  12 +-
 src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx    | 145 +++++++----------------
 src/components/editor/EditorBottomToolbar.tsx    |  29 ++---
 src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx        |  25 ++--
 src/components/editor/toolbar/MapScopeButton.tsx |  70 +++++++++++   (new)
 src/components/editor/toolbar/MenuPrimitives.tsx |   5 +
 src/lib/map/__tests__/placement.test.ts          |  58 +++------

Gates: vitest 137 files / 1091 pass / 3 skip · eslint clean · tsc --noEmit clean.

Demo (covers this task and #664): .playwright-mcp/demo/591/video-591-outer-buildings.mp4 — the scope menu's three labels, and the same drag under All Buildings vs Selected Building. Measured in 591/verify-drag.mjs: All Buildings moves the other building by 3.038e-3°, Selected Building by 0.000e+0°.

issues.display_title: Issue #664: Editor Map: other buildings as clickable outer shells, no Overview state (PRD #591 R1-R22)
issues.main_description_html:
In Editor Map mode a multi-building project shows one building at a time. The others only appear when the user zooms far enough out for useAutoOutdoor to flip the whole map to massing (src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx:107), and that view is edit-disabled — so the creator either sees indoor detail with no site context, or site context they cannot touch.

PRD #591 R1-R22 removes that trade-off: the selected building always stays indoors, every other building renders as a named outer shell alongside it, and clicking a shell switches to that building. Editor Map mode gets no Overview state and never shows every building as a shell.

The machinery already exists — preview grew it in #608/#609. outdoorGeoJson takes a buildingIds filter (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:915) and useOutdoorLayer already accepts shellBuildingIds + onSelectBuilding (src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:404). This task points the editor at the same layer instead of the zoom watcher. Preview and live behaviour must not change (R8).

Design branch design/editor-map-outer-buildings carries a version of this against a 69-commit-old base; it renders shells via setFilter/excludeBuildingId and bakes canvas label chips. Reuse the current shellBuildingIds path rather than reintroducing the old one.

Scope

  • src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx — drop useAutoOutdoor; mount useOutdoorLayer with the non-selected buildings; wire shell click to selectBuilding
  • src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts — remove outdoorMode / setOutdoorMode (only the two editor toolbars read it; preview keeps its own local state)
  • src/components/editor/EditorBottomToolbar.tsx, MapTransformControl.tsx — drop the outdoor-disabled branches
  • src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts — a press on a shell selects the building instead of starting a drag (R22)
  • Tests: shell list excludes the selected building and follows selection; shell click selects, empty-map click does not

Depends on the placement-scope task (same files).

Acceptance

  • Selected building renders indoors; every other building renders as an outer shell with its name (R2, R3, R11)
  • Shells hide indoor rooms, walls, markers, shapes, safety annotations, panorama markers and indoor labels (R10)
  • Editor Map mode never enters Overview and never shows all buildings as shells, at any zoom (R5, R6)
  • Clicking a shell selects that building; the building selector and active floor follow (R15-R19)
  • Clicking empty map space, or the already-selected building, changes nothing (R20, R21)
  • In move mode, a click on another building's shell selects only — the same gesture does not drag it (R22)
  • Preview and live outdoor behaviour unchanged (R8)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Branch: feature/664-editor-outer-buildings (stacked on feature/663-map-placement-scopes) · Commits: 108cdec, d0f91b4

Editor Map no longer has a zoom threshold. useAutoOutdoor is gone from Editor3DMapView, and with it the outdoorMode store flag the bottom toolbar and the transform popup used to refuse to edit in — there is no state to refuse in any more (R5/R6). The selected building stays indoors and every other building is a permanent context shell.

The shell layer is the one preview grew in #608 — shellBuildingIds plus select-on-click — so preview and live behaviour are untouched (R8). The list comes from outerBuildingIds, which is viewerBuildingSplit with Overview, routes and hover preview all off: sharing the rule means the editor can never shell the building it is editing (R21). Empty on a single-building project, so nothing is drawn.

In move mode a press on a shell selects only (R22): hitsGuardLayer bails before the drag disables dragPan, and the shell layer's own click handler switches buildings. Hovering a shell now restores the cursor it replaced instead of clearing it, which used to leave move mode looking disarmed.

Bug found while recording the demo, fixed here (d0f91b4): no outer building has ever shown its name — not in Editor Map, and not in the preview Overview that shipped the shells in #608. The label feature was built as a LineString whose two vertices are the same coordinate, and geojson-vt simplifies a zero-length line out of existence, so it never reached a tile. querySourceFeatures on the outdoor source said it plainly: 41 shell features, zero labels. It is a Point now; queryRenderedFeatures on the label layer returns "Community Centre Demo" and it is on screen in the demo (R11). The fix lands in preview too.
